\chapter{What Did You Say?}
\label{ch:hi-what-did-you-say}
\hlchaptermodality{126}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask what someone said, ask for it once more, and say I did not understand or do not know.}

Complete HI-C126-ek-bar-aur: keep a conversation going when you are lost.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{फिर} \hi{से} (phir se)}{फिर से (phir se)}]{\hi{फिर} \hi{से} (phir se) — once more, over again}

\label{lesson:HI-C126-phirse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for I don't feel like it, then the Hindi for fun.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{फिर} \hi{से}}
\textbf{\hi{फिर} \hi{से}} (\emph{phir se}) — \textquotedblleft{}once more\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}from the start again\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{फिर} \hi{से} \hi{बोलिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}please say it again\textquotedblright{}, a softer cousin of \textbf{\hi{दोबारा}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{फिर} \hi{से}} (\emph{phir se}) is \emph{phir}, \textquotedblleft{}again\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{se}. CDIAL lists \emph{phir} under a reconstructed \emph{*phirati}, \textquotedblleft{}turns\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9078).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second way to ask again.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phir se}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phir se}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{phir se bolie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for I don't feel like it, then the Hindi for fun, then say \emph{phir se} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{फिर} \hi{से} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Once more, over again\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया} (samajh nahīṁ āyā)}{समझ नहीं आया (samajh nahīṁ āyā)}]{\hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया} (samajh nahīṁ āyā) — I didn't understand}

\label{lesson:HI-C126-samajhnahin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for fun, then the Hindi for once more.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया}}
\textbf{\hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया}} (\emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā}) — \textquotedblleft{}I didn't understand\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}understanding did not come\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{समझ}} is \textquotedblleft{}understanding\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\hi{समझना}}. It comes, or it doesn't.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया}} (\emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā}) is \textquotedblleft{}understanding did not come\textquotedblright{}. \emph{samajh} comes from Sanskrit \emph{saṁbudhyate}, \textquotedblleft{}wakes up, understands\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12959).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The honest sentence every learner needs.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for fun, then the Hindi for once more, then say \emph{samajh nahīṁ āyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{समझ} \hi{नहीं} \hi{आया} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I didn't understand\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}? (kyā kahā?)}{क्या कहा? (kyā kahā?)}]{\hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}? (kyā kahā?) — what did you say?}

\label{lesson:HI-C126-kyakaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for once more, then the Hindi for I didn't understand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}?}
\textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}?} (\emph{kyā kahā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what did you say?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{कहा}} is the past of \textbf{\hi{कहना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}. Short, and fine among friends; with a stranger, add \textbf{\hi{जी}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}?} (\emph{kyā kahā?}) is \textquotedblleft{}what was said?\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kahnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}, comes from Sanskrit \emph{kathayati}, \textquotedblleft{}converses with, describes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2703).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A quick request to hear it again.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā kahā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā kahā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kyā kahā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for once more, then the Hindi for I didn't understand, then say \emph{kyā kahā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{क्या} \hi{कहा}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What did you say?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता} (mujhe nahīṁ patā)}{मुझे नहीं पता (mujhe nahīṁ patā)}]{\hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता} (mujhe nahīṁ patā) — I don't know}

\label{lesson:HI-C126-nahinpata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for I didn't understand, then the Hindi for what did you say.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता}}
\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता}} (\emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā}) — \textquotedblleft{}I don't know\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}to me there is no knowing\textquotedblright{}.

The person sits in \textbf{\hi{मुझे}}, the way it does for wanting and liking.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता}} (\emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā}) is \textquotedblleft{}to me no knowledge\textquotedblright{}. The origin of \emph{patā}, \textquotedblleft{}knowledge, address\textquotedblright{}, is uncertain; CDIAL does not list it, though it lists \emph{patyānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{pratyaya}, \textquotedblleft{}belief\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8640).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An honest answer to a question you cannot answer.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for I didn't understand, then the Hindi for what did you say, then say \emph{mujhe nahīṁ patā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{मुझे} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पता} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I don't know\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और} (ek bār aur)}{एक बार और (ek bār aur)}]{\hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और} (ek bār aur) — one more time}

\label{lesson:HI-C126-ekbaraur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for what did you say, then the Hindi for I don't know.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और}}
\textbf{\hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और}} (\emph{ek bār aur}) — \textquotedblleft{}one more time\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{एक}}, \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{\hi{बार}}, \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{\hi{और}}, \textquotedblleft{}more\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और} \hi{बोलिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}say it one more time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और}} (\emph{ek bār aur}) is \textquotedblleft{}one time more\textquotedblright{}. \emph{bār} comes from Sanskrit \emph{vāra}, \textquotedblleft{}one's turn\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11547), and \emph{aur}, \textquotedblleft{}more\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{apara}, \textquotedblleft{}other\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 434).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Once more, didn't understand, what did you say, don't know, one more time.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek bār aur}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek bār aur}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ek bār aur bolie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for what did you say, then the Hindi for I don't know, then say \emph{ek bār aur} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{एक} \hi{बार} \hi{और} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}One more time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
